steps: The coordinator asks every participant to prepare transaction TX.
Each yes-voter durably reserves resources and promises it can commit.
After all yes votes, the coordinator durably records commit; otherwise abort.
Participants repeatedly receive and apply that final decision during recovery.

lesson.scenario: A travel desk atomically books the last seat and a hotel room for trip TX-42.
entities: records the durable global decision for TX-42

steps.title: Begin one global booking
steps.narration: The coordinator assigns TX-42 before either supplier changes visible availability.
steps.outcome: Both resources remain sellable until prepare requests arrive.
steps.invariant: No participant may commit TX-42 without a durable global decision.

steps.title: Prepare the flight
steps.narration: Flight inventory durably reserves seat 12A and promises not to give it to another transaction.
steps.outcome: Seat 12A is locked even though the trip is not committed.
steps.invariant: A YES vote means the participant can later commit despite a restart.

steps.title: Prepare the hotel
steps.narration: Hotel inventory writes its prepared record and holds room 504.
steps.outcome: Every participant has voted YES, but prepared locks still block competing buyers.
steps.invariant: The coordinator chooses COMMIT only after every required YES vote.

steps.title: Make commit durable
steps.narration: The coordinator appends COMMIT before telling suppliers, so recovery cannot choose a different answer.
steps.outcome: TX-42 is committed logically even before all acknowledgements arrive.
steps.invariant: Once logged, the global decision is immutable and replayable.

steps.title: Finish after a lost message
steps.narration: The flight learns COMMIT immediately; the hotel learns the same decision from recovery replay.
steps.outcome: The traveler owns both reservations; retries cannot split the decision.
steps.invariant: All prepared participants eventually apply the same logged outcome.

production.scenario: A corporate travel booking service atomically reserves a hotel room and captures payment across company-owned databases.
components: Employees and coordinators submitting hotel bookings
Boundary service that validates policy and starts the booking workflow
Black-box atomic transaction service for the booking workflow
Authoritative room hold and allocation records
Durable workflow record of the global booking outcome
Worker that replays unresolved booking outcomes until every participant acknowledges
flows: An employee asks the travel portal to reserve a room and pay for it.
The booking API starts one atomic workflow for room inventory and payment.
The coordinator asks the inventory database to durably stage the room hold.
The coordinator asks the payment ledger to durably stage the charge.
Once both sides respond, the global outcome is recorded in the durable decision log.
The recovery worker continuously looks for bookings whose final outcome still needs delivery.
If the coordinator disappears mid-flight, the worker redelivers the durable outcome to inventory.
The same recovery path completes or unwinds the charge in the payment ledger.
